tagline: Open-source document lifecycle platform for drafting, reviewing and producing structured business documents.
description: Wraft is a document authoring and lifecycle tool for business content such as letters and contracts. Documents are built on open formats, Markdown and JSON, and PDFs are produced through Pandoc and LaTeX. The backend is written in Elixir with Phoenix, data lives in PostgreSQL and files go to S3-compatible storage. The developer docs describe self-hosting with Docker Compose, Kamal and Kubernetes. The repository's compose file starts the front end and back end, PostgreSQL, an S3-compatible object store and a Typesense search service. An API reference is published for integrations. The licence is AGPLv3, and the project is a product of Functionary Labs. A hosted Wraft Cloud also exists, so the open source release is one of two ways to use it. It is useful to people who want templates and a controlled workflow for documents, in the same area as DocuSign or similar document tools. The project is young and small. Check the docs for the exact feature set before planning a migration from a signing service.
strengths: Stores content in Markdown and JSON, so documents stay readable outside the tool
Produces PDFs through Pandoc and LaTeX
Documents three self-hosting routes: Docker Compose, Kamal and Kubernetes
Publishes an API reference for integrations and automation
Backed by PostgreSQL and S3-compatible storage rather than a proprietary store
limits: The compose file adds an S3-compatible store and a Typesense search service, so a full install has many parts
PDF output depends on Pandoc and LaTeX being available
The README and developer overview do not list an e-signature feature, so it may not replace a signing service
The project is small and recent, with a codebase that dates from September 2024
bestFor: A small business or developer team with a server that wants templated business documents in open formats and can run Docker.
